summary_1: Koeleria is a genus of plants in the grass family that is found on all continents except Antarctica and on various oceanic islands. Since Africa is one of the continents where Koeleria is found, the answer to the first part of the question is yes. The second part of the question asks if Koeleria is found all over, which is not accurate as Koeleria is not present in all regions of the continents where it is found.
summary_2: Virgilia is a genus of Southern African trees, indicating that it is indeed found in Africa. Koeleria, on the other hand, is found on all continents except Antarctica and on various oceanic islands, including Africa. However, Koeleria is not found all over, as it is not present in all regions of the continents where it is found.
hop1_paragraphs: Koeleria is a common and widespread genus of plants in the grass family, found on all continents except Antarctica and on various oceanic islands.  It includes species known generally as Junegrasses.
hop2_paragraphs: Virgilia is a genus of Southern African trees in the family Fabaceae, having shiny to hairy pinnate leaves and attractive mauve to pink pea-shaped flowers followed by leathery pods.  They are valued as useful ornamental trees by gardeners, particularly the well-known species "Virgilia divaricata" ('Tree in a Hurry', 'Cape Lilac', 'Blossom Tree') and "Virgilia oroboides" ('Pink Blossom Tree'), despite having a comparatively short life (15 years).  They prefer well drained soils; some will then grow 2m in the first season.  They will tolerate wind and have dense foliage growing close to the ground, so they are useful as pioneer species for privacy and wind protection.  The common name in South Africa (in Afrikaans) is keurboom, meaning 'choice tree'.
